_purpose: How the COORDINATING CENTRE combines site bundles. Read by code/pool_sites.R only; no site consumes it. Deliberately NOT in PROTOCOL_FILES: sites do not run the pooling, and putting it there would make a pooling-method edit bump the protocol version and force every site to re-run. It is stamped onto the pooled outputs instead.
_authority: Every entry implements a row of docs/cohort_and_outputs.md section 8 and names which one in its _why. If this file and that section disagree, the section is the specification and this file is the bug.
_consumption_contract: pool_sites.R MUST iterate the keys of `files` and MUST assert that every CSV present in a bundle is claimed by exactly one entry. A hardcoded list of filenames in the script would mean a newly shipped export is silently never pooled -- the first config-integrity failure mode in CLAUDE.md, one level up.
_heterogeneity_min_k_why: tau-squared needs roughly 5-10 groups to be stable, and random-effects intervals are anti-conservative below that even with Hartung-Knapp. Below this k the statistics are COMPUTED AND SHIPPED but flagged reportable = FALSE: the numbers are never hidden, only their use is governed, so they can be watched stabilising as sites arrive and the day k reaches the threshold nothing needs building.
_site_label_rule_why: Anonymised labels for audience-facing output: Site 1, Site 2, ... assigned by sorting site_name. Declared so the mapping is REPRODUCIBLE without being published, and stated in every caption. Real institution names appear only on a title page.
_exposure_display_labels_why: AUDIENCE-FACING NAMES for the two exposures, used as the panel titles on the pooled figures. 'P(indicated)' and 'P(bolus)' are working shorthand: they are not defined in a 400-word abstract and are not standard terms, so a reader meets them cold. The KEY ORDER IS THE DISPLAY ORDER -- Pindicated first, because it is the primary and the significant finding, and a reader should meet it before the null. Keyed on the UNSCALED exposure names so this cannot drift from protocol.json model.outcome_model.exposures; pool_figures.R asserts every declared exposure has a label.

01_cohort/cohort_construction.csv._why: Cohort CONSTRUCTION: the CLIF extract down to the analytic cohort. Renamed from strobe.csv on 2026-10-28, when 07 took over the STROBE -- two files called strobe.csv in one bundle was ambiguous, and this one only covers the trunk. Counts sum across sites.
01_cohort/cohort_construction.csv._caveat: The landmark row here applies the landmark to the WHOLE analytic cohort. 07's STROBE applies it AFTER the escalation restriction, so the two report different numbers for what reads like the same step -- which is why 07 drops this row from its trunk rather than showing both.

01_cohort/diagnostics/diagnostics.csv._why: Counts, summable. Grain VARIES BY ROW -- some rows are episodes, some windows, some ADT intervals -- so a pooled row is only meaningful against its own label. Summed and labelled, never divided by anything.

01_cohort/diagnostics/missingness.csv._why: Section 8.4: NOT pooled. It is the site-comparability diagnostic -- the thing you read to decide whether pooling is honest at all -- so pooling it would destroy its purpose.

01_cohort/diagnostics/missingness_patter._why: Same as missingness.csv. Also unpoolable in practice: the pattern key is a pipe-joined variable list, so a site with a different site_optional instrument has different keys.

01_cohort/exemplar_selection.csv._why: Section 8.4: the exemplar is drawn at ONE site. Four exemplars are four anecdotes, so the selection funnel describes that site alone.

02_descriptive/pooling_continuous.csv._why: Section 8.4: exact pooled mean and SD from n, sum and sum_sq. This is why sum_sq ships at all -- it assumes nothing about equal variances. Medians travel alongside and are NOT pooled; the histogram carries the pooled distribution.

02_descriptive/pooling_histograms.csv._why: Section 8.4: a median has no closed form across sites, so eight skewed or zero-inflated variables ship an absolute-bin histogram instead. n_total is OBSERVED VALUES, not windows -- pair it with missingness.csv, never with a window count.
02_descriptive/pooling_histograms.csv._numerator: observed values falling in that bin
02_descriptive/pooling_histograms.csv._denominator: n_total -- OBSERVED VALUES of that variable, not windows
02_descriptive/pooling_histograms.csv._caveat: A median has no closed form across sites, so skewed and zero-inflated variables ship a histogram on config-declared absolute bins. Pair it with missingness.csv, never with a window count. Pooled quantiles are approximate to within a bin width, except where exact zero has its own bin.

02_descriptive/retention.csv._why: Section 8.3: the denominator is the anchor cohort FIXED at every window, so it comes from cohort_construction.csv rather than from this file. Clustered within episodes.
02_descriptive/retention.csv._title: Retention on ventilation over the window grid
02_descriptive/retention.csv._numerator: episodes still ventilated in window w
02_descriptive/retention.csv._denominator: the anchor cohort, FIXED at every window

02_descriptive/dose_summary.csv._why: Section 8.3: numerator is windows with dose > 0, denominator is VENTILATED windows in that window -- not alive-admitted. n_receiving was added 2026-10-04 precisely so this pools by summing. The mean/sd columns are NOT pooled here; pooling_continuous carries the sufficient statistics for them.
02_descriptive/dose_summary.csv._not_poolable_why: This file ships a mean with NO sum_sq, so a pooled mean cannot be formed from it. pooling_continuous.csv carries the sufficient statistics for the same variables and is where the pooled central tendency comes from.
02_descriptive/dose_summary.csv._title: Share of windows receiving each drug
02_descriptive/dose_summary.csv._denominator: VENTILATED windows in w -- not alive-admitted
02_descriptive/dose_summary.csv._caveat: The receivers_only rows carry no percentage by design: that subset is already filtered to dose > 0, so a 100 there would be structural.

02_descriptive/balanced_panels.csv._why: Section 8.3: denominator is episodes ventilated in the window ENDING at h. Same treatment as dose_summary -- proportion pools, central tendency does not.
02_descriptive/balanced_panels.csv._not_poolable_why: This file ships a mean with NO sum_sq, so a pooled mean cannot be formed from it. pooling_continuous.csv carries the sufficient statistics for the same variables and is where the pooled central tendency comes from.
02_descriptive/balanced_panels.csv._denominator: episodes ventilated in the window ENDING at h

02_descriptive/imv_encounter_duration.cs._why: Quantiles only, with no sufficient statistics, so nothing here pools. The poolable view of the same variable is the first-IMV-episode histogram in pooling_histograms.csv.

04_states/state_prevalence.csv._why: Section 8.3: denominator is ALL anchor episodes with terminal states carried forward, so it is fixed and comes from cohort_construction.csv. Rows sum to 100% within a window -- verified -- which is also why a suppressed cell here would break the total.
04_states/state_prevalence.csv._numerator: episodes in that state in window w
04_states/state_prevalence.csv._denominator: all anchor episodes, with terminal states carried forward
04_states/state_prevalence.csv._caveat: Rows sum to 100% within a window, which is why the denominator is self-contained and why a suppressed cell here would break the total.

04_states/state_transition_counts.csv._why: Section 8.3 transition level: n_at_risk is transitions ORIGINATING in that state, not episodes. Excludes absorbing origins and the final window. The long count form exists so the matrix pools by summing; the wide form is the readable twin.
04_states/state_transition_counts.csv._denominator: n_at_risk -- transitions ORIGINATING in that state, not episodes
04_states/state_transition_counts.csv._caveat: Excludes absorbing origins and the final window.

04_states/state_transitions.csv._why: The WIDE readable twin of the count file above. Pooling it would double-count the same transitions; pool the long form and re-widen if a reader wants the matrix.

04_states/dose_state_prevalence.csv._why: Section 8.3: denominator is ALL anchor episodes with terminal states carried forward, so it is fixed and comes from cohort_construction.csv. Rows sum to 100% within a window -- verified -- which is also why a suppressed cell here would break the total.
04_states/dose_state_prevalence.csv._numerator: episodes in that dose band in window w
04_states/dose_state_prevalence.csv._denominator: all anchor episodes, terminal states carried forward

04_states/dose_state_transition_counts.c._why: Section 8.3 transition level: n_at_risk is transitions ORIGINATING in that state, not episodes. Excludes absorbing origins and the final window. The long count form exists so the matrix pools by summing; the wide form is the readable twin.
04_states/dose_state_transition_counts.c._denominator: n_at_risk -- transitions originating in that band

04_states/dose_state_transitions.csv._why: The WIDE readable twin of the count file above. Pooling it would double-count the same transitions; pool the long form and re-widen if a reader wants the matrix.

04_states/state_prevalence_at_risk.csv._why: Same numerator as state_prevalence, different denominator: VENTILATED only, which shrinks 14,897 -> 10,999 -> 8,146 -> 6,728. The pair is the point; pooling one without the other loses the distinction between 'of everyone' and 'of those still at risk'.
04_states/state_prevalence_at_risk.csv._title: Delivery-state prevalence among those still at risk
04_states/state_prevalence_at_risk.csv._denominator: VENTILATED episodes only, so it shrinks window by window
04_states/state_prevalence_at_risk.csv._caveat: The pair is the point: one answers 'of everyone', the other 'of those still at risk'.

05_titration/coadministration.csv._why: Section 8.3 event level: events with a fentanyl bolus within +/-30 min, over events in that group, restricted to ventilated windows. CLUSTERED in episodes -- the point estimate is exact, the naive binomial interval is not. Carry deff.
05_titration/coadministration.csv._title: Bolus co-administration at a fentanyl rate increase
05_titration/coadministration.csv._grain: event, clustered within episodes; emitted per cohort (all | landmark)
05_titration/coadministration.csv._numerator: rate-change events with a fentanyl bolus charted within +/-30 min
05_titration/coadministration.csv._denominator: rate-change events of that kind, ventilated windows only
05_titration/coadministration.csv._caveat: `any increase` = initiation union uptitration; downtitration is the NEGATIVE CONTROL and is excluded from it. `deff` is blank in the pooled row on purpose: it describes clustering within ONE site's episodes, so averaging two of them would describe nothing. The point estimate pools exactly; the interval does not. EACH ROW APPEARS TWICE, under cohort = all and cohort = landmark. `all` is the whole analytic cohort; `landmark` is the subset still on IMV at T = 72h, the only population the outcome analysis can speak for. Read them side by side -- the gap is the selection -- and never add them, because landmark is a subset of all.
05_titration/coadministration.csv._cohort_key_why: A KEY, NOT A LABEL. `landmark` is a SUBSET of `all`, so summing the two rows -- which every sum_counts method does across whatever it is not keyed on -- would count every landmark event twice. Carrying cohort in `keys` makes the pooled table report the two strata side by side, which is the comparison SG asked for on 2026-10-27: the descriptive epidemiology belongs to the whole cohort, the outcome analysis can only speak for the landmark subset, and the gap between them IS the selection bias the paper has to declare.

05_titration/indication.csv._why: Section 8.3: THREE proportions share this row and two share a numerator. pct_indicated_all is n_indicated/n_events; pct_indicated_of_assessed is the SAME numerator over n_assessed. Both must be recomputed from summed counts, never averaged.
05_titration/indication.csv._title: Was the escalation indicated? Documented pain or agitation nearby
05_titration/indication.csv._grain: event, clustered within episodes; emitted per cohort (all | landmark)
05_titration/indication.csv._numerator: pct_assessed: events with ANY score of that class within the window. pct_indicated_all: events with a score AT OR ABOVE that instrument's threshold
05_titration/indication.csv._denominator: events of that type. pct_indicated_of_assessed uses n_assessed instead, which is what separates documentation from indication
05_titration/indication.csv._caveat: THE PAIN CLASS IS NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS SITES that chart different instruments: cpot_total >= 3 on a 0-8 scale and NVPS >= 4 on a 0-10 scale do not mark the same severity, and they behave differently under the window sweep. The SEDATION class uses RASS >= +1 everywhere and is the clean cross-site comparison. 05_titration/diagnostics/indication_wind._why: The 1-4h sweep of the row above. Pools identically. A result that appears only at the widest window is measuring assessment cadence, not indication -- which is why the sweep is pooled rather than only the primary window.
05_titration/diagnostics/indication_wind._numerator: as indication.csv, swept over W = 1-4 h
05_titration/diagnostics/indication_wind._caveat: Widening the window buys more ASSESSED events faster than more INDICATED ones, so the level rises with W at every site. The primary window is 1 h.
05_titration/diagnostics/indication_wind._relocated: Moved from 05_titration/ into 05_titration/diagnostics/ on 2026-10-27 so the phase directory holds only what we report directly. Still shipped, still pooled -- the split is editorial. A site running an older tag emits it at the old path and pool_sites.R will refuse the bundle as unclaimed, which is the intended loud failure.

05_titration/assessment_frequency.csv._not_poolable_why: The gap quantiles are quantiles and do not pool; they are the per-site answer and the RANGE across sites is the thing to report. records_per_ventilated_day is blanked here but IS recoverable at the centre: sum(n_records) / (sum(n_ventilated_windows) * window_hours / 24). It is left blank rather than summed because the engine has no generic path to a rate whose denominator is a unit conversion of another column.
05_titration/assessment_frequency.csv._why: Answers the reviewer objection that a low indicated fraction reflects missing documentation rather than absent pain. Keyed by INSTRUMENT, so n_ventilated_windows repeats across the rows of one site and sums correctly across sites within an instrument -- no double counting. The denominator is VENTILATED windows, matching the indication analysis; missingness.csv counts the same scores over ALIVE-ADMITTED windows, which is 1.36x larger at UCMC, and setting the two side by side without noticing that looks like a contradiction.
05_titration/assessment_frequency.csv._title: How often is a score documented at all?
05_titration/assessment_frequency.csv._numerator: ventilated windows containing at least one score of that instrument
05_titration/assessment_frequency.csv._denominator: that site's ventilated windows, RESTRICTED TO THE SAME COHORT as the numerator -- landmark records over landmark ventilated windows. Dividing landmark records by the whole cohort's windows would report a cadence about 2x too sparse.
05_titration/assessment_frequency.csv._caveat: An instrument charted at only ONE site pools to that site's own value by construction -- it is not a two-site estimate. The denominator is VENTILATED windows; missingness.csv counts the same scores over ALIVE-ADMITTED windows, which is larger, so quoting the two together without saying so looks contradictory. 05_titration/diagnostics/window_sensitiv._why: The 5-60 min bolus-window sweep. Same grain and same clustering as coadministration.
05_titration/diagnostics/window_sensitiv._numerator: events with a bolus within W minutes
05_titration/diagnostics/window_sensitiv._caveat: A result that holds only at the widest window is measuring charting cadence rather than practice. Read the ORDERING across widths, not the level.
05_titration/diagnostics/window_sensitiv._relocated: Moved from 05_titration/ into 05_titration/diagnostics/ on 2026-10-27 so the phase directory holds only what we report directly. 05_titration/diagnostics/charting_precis._why: Whether the pairing survives when the charted action label is required to agree. A measurement-quality check, poolable by summing.
05_titration/diagnostics/charting_precis._title: Does pairing survive on timestamps charted on the hour?
05_titration/diagnostics/charting_precis._numerator: events paired with a bolus within W minutes
05_titration/diagnostics/charting_precis._denominator: events in that on-the-hour / off-the-hour class

05_titration/diagnostics/charting_agreem._why: Counts of charted action label against the rate delta that defines the event. Summable.

05_titration/adherence_distribution.csv._why: Section 8.3: denominator is n_episodes_ge_min_events (>= 2 increases), NOT n_episodes. Getting that wrong inflates the denominator with episodes that could not have adhered.
05_titration/adherence_distribution.csv._title: Per-episode share of increases that were paired
05_titration/adherence_distribution.csv._numerator: pct_never: episodes at exactly 0. pct_always: episodes at exactly 1
05_titration/adherence_distribution.csv._denominator: n_episodes_ge_min_events -- episodes with at least 2 increases, NOT n_episodes
05_titration/adherence_distribution.csv._caveat: A single-event episode can only score 0 or 1, which would pile artificial mass at both ends of a distribution meant to describe a tendency. The word 'adherence' asserts a standard that no evidence here establishes. EACH ROW APPEARS TWICE, under cohort = all and cohort = landmark. `all` is the whole analytic cohort; `landmark` is the subset still on IMV at T = 72h, the only population the outcome analysis can speak for. 05_titration/rate_change_magnitude.csv._why: Restructured 2026-10-05 from a column named mcg_per_hr that held percentages. The share-at-or-above rows pool by summing; the quantile rows do not and are carried as a range.

05_titration/pooling_histograms.csv._why: The two histograms emitted by 05 rather than 02: rate-change magnitude and per-episode adherence. Identical treatment to the 02 file.
05_titration/pooling_histograms.csv._numerator: observed values falling in that bin
05_titration/pooling_histograms.csv._denominator: n_total -- observed values of that variable

06_unit_variation/unit_adherence.csv._why: SECTION 8.7: NEVER SUMMED BY LABEL, but shipped and used. No pooled row is keyed by a unit name, because the names have no cross-site correspondence. The rows are instead the INPUT to the between-site dispersion statistic and to the replication caterpillar and funnel, where every unit from every site is a point under an anonymised label -- the finer location_name grouping gives 9 units at UCMC against care_setting's 7, and is where the spread shows most. Per-site rows pass through unchanged, with real names.
06_unit_variation/unit_adherence.csv._unit_keys_not_summed_why: BOTH keys, not just location_name. A unit NAME has no counterpart at another site -- UCMC's N03B is not Rush's anything, and care_setting level sets differ by site by construction -- so no pooled row is ever keyed by a unit. The per-site rows pass through with their REAL names, because the centre needs them to sanity-check a site's own grouping and because a ward code is not PHI (SG, 2026-10-26). Anonymisation happens at figure time for an audience, not here. This key replaced one named unit_keys_internal_only, which was both inaccurate -- these rows ship in the upload set -- and DEAD, read by nothing. Listing them is documentation; the engine enforces it through method = heterogeneity_source, which has no summing path at all.
06_unit_variation/unit_adherence.csv._care_setting_column_why: Added 2026-10-26. A location_name row and a care_setting row are separate row sets with nothing linking them, and the mapping lives only in care_intervals.parquet, which is PHI-side -- so the centre cannot derive it and the site has to emit it. This column is what lets the combined, anonymised location_name panel be coloured by CARE SETTING instead of by site, which shows whether medical ICUs cluster high ACROSS hospitals rather than merely that units vary. A care_setting row carries its own setting; a location_name row carries the one it maps to, or 'multiple' where a ward was reclassified mid-period. Part of the key, not a summable column: nothing is ever summed across a unit name.

06_unit_variation/year_adherence.csv._why: Section 8.4: the year series is per site. Calendar coverage differs, and a conversion such as MIMIC may carry shifted dates, so a pooled year curve would mix eras.

06_unit_variation/attribution_funnel.csv._why: How many events were attributable to a care location at all. Summable, and worth pooling: the unattributed share is a data-quality contrast between sites.

06_unit_variation/overdispersion.csv._why: The WITHIN-site dispersion of units inside that hospital. Not pooled: the between-SITE statistic is computed fresh by pool_sites.R from unit_adherence.csv using the same overdispersion() in utils/pooling.R, grouped by site instead of by unit. Carrying both side by side is the actual finding -- variation within a hospital, and between them.

07_outcome_model/model_coefficients.csv._why: THE POOLING PAYLOAD. Each site fits the ordinal model locally and ships the coefficients; the centre combines them by inverse variance. A two-stage meta-analysis, NOT pooled individual data. estimate/std_error/ci_* are LOG ODDS, which is the scale that pools; odds_ratio/or_ci_* are the exponentiated version for reading and must never be averaged.
07_outcome_model/model_coefficients.csv._grain: admission; one row per model per term
07_outcome_model/model_coefficients.csv._numerator: n/a -- this is a regression coefficient, not a count
07_outcome_model/model_coefficients.csv._denominator: n_admissions, the complete-case count for that model
07_outcome_model/model_coefficients.csv._caveat: ONLY ROWS WITH poolable = TRUE MAY BE COMBINED. The ICU fixed effects are blanked at the site: location_name is site-local free text, so an `icuMICU` coefficient names nothing at another site. The thresholds are not shipped at all -- they depend on each site's covariate distribution and are not the same quantity across sites. The pooled estimand is therefore the WITHIN-SITE, ICU-ADJUSTED association. With k below heterogeneity_min_k the fixed-effect estimate is primary and tau-squared is descriptive only. A model with converged = FALSE in model_diagnostics.csv MUST BE EXCLUDED.
07_outcome_model/model_coefficients.csv._not_poolable_why: n_units counts the ICU fixed effects FITTED AT THAT SITE. location_name is site-local free text, so the units are not shared and a sum would count (site, unit) pairs while reading as a number of units -- and the pooled estimand is the WITHIN-SITE, ICU-adjusted association, which makes each site's unit count a property of that site rather than of the pool. n_admissions does sum, because an admission means the same thing everywhere.

07_outcome_model/model_covariance.csv._why: The 2x2 between the two exposures, so the centre can test them JOINTLY rather than one at a time -- shipping standard errors alone forecloses that. POOLED WITH THE SAME WEIGHTS the coefficients used: under site independence Cov(b1_bar, b2_bar) = sum_i(w1_i*w2_i*Cov_i) / (sum w1 * sum w2). The diagonal must reproduce the pooled variances, which pool_covariance_meta asserts rather than assumes. REQUIRES paired_with to have been pooled first, because the weights come from there; pool_sites.R fails loudly if it has not.
07_outcome_model/model_covariance.csv._caveat: Only cells whose BOTH terms pooled are produced -- a term dropped at one site has no weight there. k_sites names how many sites backed each cell and may be lower than for the coefficients.

07_outcome_model/exposure_distribution.c._why: Counts on FIXED bins of width 0.05, which pool by addition. A kernel density would not. Both exposures are proportions with a large point mass at zero, so the bin holding zero carries most of the cohort and the shape is in the tail.
07_outcome_model/exposure_distribution.c._caveat: The bin containing 0 includes exactly 0, which is 68% of Pbolus and 50% of Pindicated at UCMC -- do not read the histogram as if mass were spread.

07_outcome_model/exposure_by_unit.csv._why: Per-unit medians and IQRs for the per-unit figure and for between-unit dispersion. Quantiles do not pool; the RANGE across units is what to report, and location_name is site-local so these rows pass through per site.
07_outcome_model/exposure_by_unit.csv._location_category_column_why: Added 2026-10-27 for protocol.json 0.13.0, alongside the icu_only sensitivity. location_name is SITE-LOCAL FREE TEXT -- 'N08S' and 'ED CCD' mean nothing at Northwestern or Rush -- so without the mCIDE location_category beside it the centre cannot tell an ICU row from an ED row, and the per-unit rows cannot be grouped into anything comparable across sites. This is not hypothetical: at UCMC the Emergency Department is the LARGEST level at 1,212 of 2,897 admissions (41.8%) while every description of the model called these 'ICU fixed effects', and that went unnoticed until the composition was measured. The column is a LABEL, not a quantity: it is functionally determined by location_name, so it is deliberately NOT added to `keys` -- the grain is still one row per (exposure, location_name) and adding it would imply a finer grain than the file has. It needs no label_columns entry either, because heterogeneity_source falls through pool_sites.R without reaching pool_sum_counts, where the label-versus-blank logic lives.
07_outcome_model/exposure_by_unit.csv._caveat: Cells below reporting.small_cell_min_den are blanked at the site. Unit names are real here and are anonymised at figure time, per the standing rule.

07_outcome_model/exposure_correlation.cs._why: The collinearity check between the two exposures. A correlation coefficient does not pool by addition and the honest combined statement is the range across sites.
07_outcome_model/exposure_correlation.cs._caveat: Report the range across sites, never a mean of correlations.

07_outcome_model/vfd_ordinal.csv._why: Counts per ordinal outcome level. Sums across sites exactly.
07_outcome_model/vfd_ordinal.csv._caveat: The bottom level is exactly 0 and holds about half the cohort. It means two different things -- died, or never liberated -- and the split between them is in time_to_event, not here.
07_outcome_model/vfd_ordinal.csv._weighted_means_why: mean_vfd_28 is the band's observed mean VFD-28, the value the adjusted expectation maps each band through (protocol.json band_values). It pools EXACTLY as sum(n_i * mean_i) / sum(n_i), because mean * n reconstructs the sum -- this is not an average of averages. The pooled mapping is what a centre-side curve would have to use; each site's own adjusted_prediction.csv keeps its own, which is why that file is heterogeneity_source.

07_outcome_model/table1.csv._why: The FORMATTED Table 1, one column per displayed cohort scope with that scope's own N in the header. Per-site by construction: the cells are strings like '60.0 (46.0, 70.0)' and the N is in the column NAME, so there is nothing here a pooling engine can combine. The poolable twin is table1_continuous.csv and table1_categorical.csv, built by the same calls from the same numbers -- see code/utils/table1.R, where each builder returns both halves at once precisely so a table and its pooling export cannot drift.
07_outcome_model/table1.csv._caveat: NO P-VALUE, and there must not be one: every displayed column is a nested subset of Overall, so a test between them compares a group with itself. See protocol.json table1._why_no_p_value. Who was excluded is answered by 07_outcome_model/strobe.csv.

07_outcome_model/table1_continuous.csv._why: The poolable half of Table 1's continuous rows: median, Q1, Q3 and n per variable per cohort scope. POOLED BY THE SAMPLE-SIZE-WEIGHTED MEDIAN OF MEDIANS (McGrath et al., Statistics in Medicine 2019, section 2.2; the paper is in references/). A median does not pool by summing and the sites do not ship the order statistics a true pooled median would need, so the weighted median of the site medians is the estimator, with weights proportional to n. The mean DOES pool exactly from n/sum/sum_sq, which this file also carries, so pooled mean and sd are reported alongside and will not agree with the pooled median on skewed variables -- that disagreement is informative, not an error.
07_outcome_model/table1_continuous.csv._interval_why: THE 95% INTERVAL IS THE RANGE OF SITE MEDIANS AT OUR k, AND THAT IS THE METHOD, NOT A SHORTCUT. McGrath's limits are the 1/2 -+ min(1/2, z/(2*sqrt(k))) weighted quantiles; measured against this implementation the interval stays pinned to the full range until k = 6. So at three sites 'WM 95% CI' and 'range of site medians' are the same two numbers and must not be reported as though they were independent. The engine flags this per row in median_is_range. McGrath's own simulations used k = 15 or 50, so three sites is outside the range the method was evaluated on; report it as a weighted median of medians with a range, not as validated inference.
07_outcome_model/table1_continuous.csv._denominator: n, the admissions in that scope at that site
07_outcome_model/table1_continuous.csv._caveat: Cells below reporting.small_cell_min_den are blanked at the site, so a site can contribute an n without contributing a median; k_sites names how many medians actually backed each pooled row. Rows in protocol.json table1.model_scope_only exist only for the model scope.

07_outcome_model/table1_categorical.csv._why: The poolable half of Table 1's categorical rows. Counts sum exactly and the percentage is recomputed from the sums, never averaged across sites. Both the collapsed levels the table displays and the raw mCIDE levels ship, so a pooled count is never lost to a display choice.
07_outcome_model/table1_categorical.csv._caveat: A suppressed cell takes the next-smallest with it, or the published denominator minus the rest would recover it. Race ships collapsed and raw; the collapsed levels are declared in protocol.json table1.race_levels.

07_outcome_model/vfd_day_distribution.cs._why: THE PRIMARY OUTCOME'S OWN DISTRIBUTION, one row per attainable whole day. Added for protocol.json 0.14.0, where outcome_scale became integer_days: a reader cannot reconstruct 24 model levels from the 4 descriptive bands in vfd_ordinal.csv, and the two files answer different questions. Counts sum across sites exactly. THE DAY GRID IS FIXED AT 0..25 AND SHIPPED IN FULL, including days with zero admissions, so the key set is identical at every site and the pooled row is a sum over the same levels rather than an outer join that invents gaps.
07_outcome_model/vfd_day_distribution.cs._numerator: admissions with that many whole ventilator-free days
07_outcome_model/vfd_day_distribution.cs._caveat: is_model_level is FALSE for a day no admission reached, which is not missing data: day 1 is unreachable by construction because a liberation must last 48h to count at all, so the smallest nonzero VFD is about two days. Day 25 is the ceiling and requires extubation at exactly the landmark hour. The floor at day 0 holds about half the cohort and means two different things -- died, or never liberated.

07_outcome_model/adjusted_prediction.csv._why: The standardised predicted mean VFD-28 and P(VFD-28 = 0) across the declared exposure grid. PASSES THROUGH PER SITE AND IS NOT POOLED, because standardisation averages over THAT SITE'S covariate distribution -- age, sex, CCI, SOFA and its own ICU fixed effects -- so two sites' curves are not estimates of one quantity and averaging them would be averaging over two different populations while looking like a meta-analysis. What DOES pool is the exposure coefficient in model_coefficients.csv, by inverse variance, which is the declared pooling route for this model (protocol.json model.outcome_model._pooling_why). A pooled curve, if the centre ever wants one, is drawn FROM the pooled coefficient against a chosen covariate distribution -- it is not built by combining these rows.
07_outcome_model/adjusted_prediction.csv._title: Adjusted predicted VFD-28 by exposure level
07_outcome_model/adjusted_prediction.csv._denominator: n_admissions, the model frame the prediction is standardised over
07_outcome_model/adjusted_prediction.csv._caveat: Intervals are bootstrap percentile intervals from MVN(coef, vcov) at the declared seed, so they are reproducible but are NOT comparable to the Wald intervals on the coefficients. The curve is an association standardised over observed covariates, not an effect: confounding by indication is unaddressed.

07_outcome_model/unadjusted_bins.csv._why: The unadjusted comparison the adjusted curve is read against: VFD-28 by binned exposure, with exactly zero split out as its own bin. THE ZERO SHARE DOES POOL and is pooled here -- n_vfd_zero and n_admissions sum, pct_vfd_zero is recomputed from the sums -- which is deliberately NOT what happens to the per-unit zero shares in exposure_by_unit.csv, left as a heterogeneity_source because its grain is a site-local unit name. Here the key is a declared bin that means the same thing at every site, so there is no reason not to pool it.
07_outcome_model/unadjusted_bins.csv._not_poolable_why: The MEANS cannot pool from what this file ships: a mean of means needs the per-bin n, sum and sum_sq that pool_sufficient consumes, and this file ships a mean and an interval instead. Declared rather than silently blanked -- pool_sum_counts stops on an undeclared numeric column for exactly this reason. mean_vfd_28 per bin is therefore a PER-SITE number; the pooled row carries the zero share and NA for the mean. If a pooled mean is ever wanted, ship n/sum/sum_sq and switch the method, do not average the means.
07_outcome_model/unadjusted_bins.csv._numerator: admissions in that bin with VFD-28 exactly zero
07_outcome_model/unadjusted_bins.csv._caveat: EXACTLY ZERO IS ITS OWN BIN because about half of admissions never have a qualifying score at any increase, so a 0-20% bin would be half the cohort and almost entirely one value. Bins below reporting.small_cell_min_den keep their counts and have every statistic blanked. Unadjusted means confound: no case mix, no unit, no severity.

07_outcome_model/diagnostics/proportiona._why: THE VERDICT OF THE GATE, as a file and not only as a console line. The partial-proportional-odds sensitivity was dropped on 2026-10-28 conditional on both exposures passing the PO test (protocol.json model.outcome_model.proportional_odds_gate), so whether that condition held at a site is part of what the site must ship -- a bundle whose gate failed is not poolable at all, and the centre needs to see that without reading a log.
07_outcome_model/diagnostics/proportiona._caveat: passed = FALSE on any row means DO NOT POOL this bundle. status = not_testable also fails: an untested assumption is not a satisfied one. The gate binds on the primary model only; a sensitivity that fails is warned about in the run log and does not halt it.

07_outcome_model/strobe.csv._why: THE STROBE: the whole funnel, trunk plus both branches, in one file. 07 ships it because it is the only script that can -- the restrictions below the analytic cohort are 05's titration events and 07's own complete-case filter and unit collapse, none of which exist when 01 runs. The trunk is read from 01_cohort/cohort_construction.csv rather than re-derived.
07_outcome_model/strobe.csv._denominator: n/a -- a flow, not a proportion
07_outcome_model/strobe.csv._caveat: Rows within a branch chain; rows ACROSS branches do not, and summing them double-counts. n_before on the first row of each branch is the analytic cohort it descends from. The last model row is the frame actually fitted, which is smaller than the complete-case count by the unit collapse.
07_outcome_model/strobe.csv._branch_why: TWO BRANCHES, NOT ONE CHAIN, because there are two denominators: practice_patterns is every admission that escalated at all and is what the per-escalation rates are over; model is the complete-case frame the regression fits. They are not nested in sequence -- both descend from the analytic cohort -- so branch is part of the key and the rows must never be summed across branches.

07_outcome_model/diagnostics/model_diagn._why: Convergence, condition number and AIC per model. NOT a result -- it is the evidence that a coefficient may be read at all. A model with converged = FALSE must be excluded from the pool.
07_outcome_model/diagnostics/model_diagn._caveat: cond_H above about 1e10 means the parameters are not uniquely determined. This caught a singular Hessian at UCMC on the first run, from a collapsed ICU level holding one admission.

07_outcome_model/diagnostics/proportiona._why: nominal_test() per term. Proportional odds is TESTED, not assumed: with half the cohort at VFD = 0 it is exactly where this model is most likely to fail, and a violated assumption means one odds ratio does not describe that term across cut points.
07_outcome_model/diagnostics/proportiona._caveat: A small p means the assumption fails for that term. Report it; do not quietly keep the odds ratio.

_label_columns_why: Columns CARRIED onto the POOLED row rather than summed or blanked. A non-numeric label that is not listed here is silently set to NA, and the undeclared-numeric guard in pool_sum_counts cannot catch it because it only inspects numeric columns -- which is exactly how is_exposure came back NA on the pooled coefficient rows and dropped them from the forest plot's own filter. If a POOLED row loses a label it should have kept, add it here.
_not_poolable_columns_why: Explicitly NA in the POOLED row, because they are quantities a sum cannot produce. A median has no closed form across sites -- the histogram carries that. A per-site confidence interval and design effect describe THAT site's clustering. pct_indicated_of_assessed has a different denominator (n_assessed) and is recomputed separately rather than summed. Leaving these blank is the honest answer; carrying one site's value into a pooled row would be a lie about what it describes. mean and sd were removed on review: they ARE poolable wherever sum and sum_sq ship, which is exactly what pooling_continuous.csv exists for. In files that carry only a mean they are unpoolable, and the engine's guard reports that per file rather than this list asserting it globally.
_per_file_not_poolable: A file entry may carry its own `not_poolable` list, unioned with the global one. Poolability is a property of what a file SHIPS, not of a column name.
_summary_contract: pool_sites.R renders output/pooled/pooled_summary.md from the _title, _grain, _numerator, _denominator and _caveat keys on each entry that declares `percents`. An entry with percents and no _numerator is a gap: the number would ship with no statement of what it counts, which is the thing the summary exists to prevent. The engine asserts it.
_care_setting_display_groups_why: PRESENTATION ONLY, for the pooled figures. Centre-side: no site reads this and it does not affect any analysis. MEASURED 2026-10-27 across UCMC and Rush: only 2 of 10 care_setting values -- ed and medical_icu -- appear at BOTH sites. The other eight are unique to one, so colouring 14 units by 10 raw settings makes the colour a site label with extra steps, which defeats the reason for using care_setting at all (seeing whether, say, medical ICUs cluster high ACROSS hospitals). Grouping to 6 comparable classes restores that reading. THE MAPPING IS A CLINICAL JUDGEMENT AND IS PROVISIONAL: whether general_icu is Medical and whether mixed_cardiothoracic_icu groups with cardiac or with surgical are SG's calls, not the code's. An unmapped value falls through to its own label rather than being silently bucketed. NOTE the grouping does not rescue comparability by itself -- at these two sites even the shared categories separate BY SITE (ED 11.5% vs 65.4%; medical ICUs 20.8-23.1% vs 26.9-45.8%), which is itself the finding: site dominates care setting.

_changelog.0.2.0: 2026-10-27, for protocol.json 0.8.0. Four 05 files gained `cohort` as their FIRST key (all | landmark). Four method checks moved to 05_titration/diagnostics/ and their spec keys moved with them. Table 1 strata changed from predominant dose band to cohort membership, so `stratum` in pooling_categorical.csv and pooling_continuous.csv takes overall | Landmark | Not landmark. A bundle from 0.1.0 WILL be refused: the moved files arrive at paths this spec does not claim, which is the intended loud failure rather than a silent partial pool.
_changelog.0.4.0: 2026-10-27, for protocol.json 0.13.0. Adds the location_category column to 07_outcome_model/exposure_by_unit.csv so a per-unit row can be identified as an ICU or an ED at the centre, where location_name is site-local free text and says nothing. No file is added or removed and no method changes; the grain of every entry is unchanged. Also records the exposure reporting unit: both 07 exposure coefficients are now per 10 PERCENTAGE POINTS of the share and the shipped term names say so (Pbolus_per10pp, Pindicated_per10pp), so coefficients from a v0.12.x bundle and a v0.13.x bundle are on DIFFERENT SCALES and must not be pooled together.
_changelog.0.3.0: 2026-10-27, for protocol.json 0.12.0. Adds the eight 07_outcome_model files. model_coefficients.csv introduces a method this spec has not carried before -- INVERSE-VARIANCE META-ANALYSIS of regression coefficients rather than summing numerators and denominators. It is declared as `coefficient_meta` and pool_sites.R does not implement it yet; the entry exists so the file is CLAIMED and a bundle carrying it is not refused, and so the contract is written down before the centre-side code is.
